messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: SLO breach detected for streaming p99 and tail latency across cross-zone egress (eu-west2 <-> us-east1). Auto-paging to #incidents. Root cause unknown, immediate triage requested.
Alejandra: seeing streaming stalls + sudden p99 jumps from ~420ms -> ~2.3s across a subset of requests, p95 also elevated. Dashboard shows spike at 08:12 UTC. Customer-facing errors increasing for long-lived streams.
Sam: noticed increased TLS handshake retransmits in the tcp traces for flows exiting via NAT-x-02 in eu-west2. Packet loss counters also ticked up on that path.
Mike: confirmed. Netmetrics: interzone packet-loss ~3.2% and retransmits spike correlated with p99 window. Logs show repeated TLS SYN retries to upstream model hosts.
Jia: is this limited to streaming endpoints or general text generate too?
Alejandra: mostly streaming tail latency and stalls; short requests (<=128 tokens) less affected but p95 drifts. Embeddings unaffected.
Tanvi: tagging oncall infra. I ran a quick `mtr` from nat-host-02 -> gateway and saw intermittent losses and ~200ms queue spikes.
Paul: possible NAT ephemeral port exhaustion? Any conntrack drops?
Sam: checked conntrack counters on nat-host-02: entries stable, but iptables conntrack-drops increased ~4.5k over 10m. Ephemeral ports look ok on host, but upstream path shows a lot of retransmits.
Alejandra: customer impact: two enterprise customers reported degraded streaming sessions (timed out or truncated responses). CS flagged 3 support tickets in the last 20m.
Mike: I grabbed packet captures around the window. Observed multiple retransmit bursts and TLS handshake timeouts before successful connect: `SYN -> SYN/ACK lost -> retransmit -> TLS handshake restart` pattern.
Jia: could be cross-zone hairpin routing causing extra hops. Any recent routing changes or ASG resizes?
Tanvi: no config changes in the last 24h. Cloud provider shows a transient NAT gateway maintenance window at 08:10 UTC in eu-west2 but status was reported green after. Might coincide.
Alejandra: mitigation idea: shift streaming traffic for eu-west2 customers to eu-west1 fallback pool and fail open to dedicated-route fallback for currently impacted routes. Also consider forcing short keepalives to avoid long-lived sockets.
Paul: agree. Quick win: add route pinning for streaming-route -> eu-west1 for the next 15m, and enable autoscale burst on dedicated pool in eu-west1. Also add 30s socket-level keepalive to reduce stuck streams.
Sam: implementing route pin now via routing-api: `POST /routes/pin {"route":"streaming-v1","destination":"eu-west1-pool"}`
Alejandra: ops-bot, please push canary and watch for errors.
ops-bot: Canary rollout started for route streaming-v1 -> eu-west1-pool (10% traffic). Health checks running.
Mike: while that's deploying, I'll open tcpdump on nat-host-02 and nat-host-03 for 5m windows and upload captures to /tmp/incidents/3123456789/pcap.
Jia: also run `dig +short @8.8.8.8 model-service.eu-west1.internal` and sanity-check DNS latency; additive DNS timeouts could exacerbate TLS handshakes.
Sam: DNS looks fine from control plane; latencies ~20ms, no NXDOMAIN.
Tanvi: can we temporarily bypass NAT for these flows? Host-level SNAT change is risky mid-prod. Alternative: route to egress-gateway in same AZ instead of cross-AZ NAT hop.
Paul: I'll spin up an emergency egress-gateway in az-b in eu-west2 and update policy to prefer local egress for pinned streaming traffic. ETA ~6m.
Alejandra: note customers on dedicated capacity should not be impacted, but multi-tenant hosted streams are. CS notified and we provided mitigation steps to affected customers: re-establish stream or use non-streaming endpoint as fallback.
Mike: capture uploaded: /tmp/incidents/3123456789/pcap/nat-02-pre-mit.pcap
ops-bot: Canary at 10% healthy. Error rate for canary shards down from 4.8% -> 1.1% after reroute.
Sam: good signal. Let's ramp to 50% then 100% if stable for 2 minutes.
Alejandra: ramping to 50%.
ops-bot: Reroute ramp to 50% complete. Health metrics showing p99 down 60% on canary shards.
Paul: egress-gateway ready in az-b, updating policy to prefer local egress for streaming-v1 pinned routes.
Tanvi: policy updated, monitoring interzone path metrics. Packet-loss on nat-x-02 dropping back toward baseline.
Mike: post-mit captures show retransmits dropped by ~85%. TLS handshake success rate up.
Alejandra: customer impact reduced; CS report: the two enterprise tickets now show reconnected streams and fewer timeouts.
Jia: root cause candidate: provider-side NAT path degradation causing transient packet loss and handshake retransmits, amplified by long-lived streaming connections and cross-zone hairpin routing. Secondary factor: conntrack spikes causing momentary drops.
Sam: follow-ups: 1) Work with provider to get postmortem for NAT gateway maintenance at 08:10 UTC. 2) Add runbook steps: automatic regional reroute when interzone packet loss >1% and p99 >1s for 2m. 3) Consider shorter default streaming keepalive and socket timeouts for hosted tiers. 4) Add telemetry alert for TLS handshake retries rate.
Alejandra: I'll own the incident postmortem and timeline. Sam, Paul, Mike, Jia — please add any logs/artifacts to the incident folder. Tanvi please own provider escalation.
Paul: noted, I'll collect conntrack histograms and egress gateway metrics.
Tanvi: contacting provider support now, including packet captures and timeline.
ops-bot: Incident severity updated to Sev2. Paging paused.
Alejandra: thanks team. Final note for timeline: created mitigation at 08:18 UTC (route pin + egress-gateway), resolved customer-facing errors by 08:24 UTC. Will post full RCA in ~2-3 hours. Reacted with :thumbsup: (Sam, Paul).
